reasoning_traces.think:
Reasoning operates by extracting partial aspects from holistic phenomena, enabling structured inference. The core mechanism is that while empirical thought aggregates all data, reasoned thought isolates relevant components—φ ⊂ Φ—that bear stronger relations to conclusions than the whole. This process is formalized as a selection operator R(Φ) → φ, where φ is chosen based on relevance ρ(φ,C). When φ fails to capture sufficient structure, inference breaks down. The dual nature of this operation lies in its ability to both reduce complexity and preserve predictive power. Failure modes include overgeneralization (φ too small) or undergeneralization (φ too large), both leading to incorrect coupling of data and conclusion. The mathematical dualism manifests in the contrast between full-data association and partial-data mediation. In GSI, this translates into Bayesian updating over extracted features; in GSE, it becomes a state-transition kernel defined by selected observables.
